entries.resolution_note: Genuine A/B split: Coder A read positive (5-star rating + constructive usage tip); Coder B read mixed (5-star satisfaction sitting alongside a workflow caveat). Resolver → mixed. Independent basis: the reviewer's own words 'works best when you work with it and do one section at a time' semantically entail that one-shot/autonomous generation works less well — a source-grounded capability caveat, not an inference added by the coder — and it co-exists with genuine 5-star satisfaction. Both a positive and a negative signal are codable from the single item, which is the §5 definition of mixed. Writer may use it both as a satisfied-user data point and as the section-by-section/needs-oversight caveat; it is NOT a clean one-sided endorsement.

coding.aspect: workflow — 5-star satisfaction (positive) + source-grounded caveat that best results need section-by-section human collaboration, entailing one-shot drafts are weaker (negative); resolved to mixed
